claims.wording: MacFlow describes itself as AI-powered environment management for macOS developers.
claims.excerpt: AI-powered environment management for macOS developers.

claims.wording: The homepage offers v1.0.15-alpha as a macOS Universal download and lists macOS 11.0+, Apple Silicon and Intel.
claims.excerpt:
macOS 11.0+ • Apple Silicon & Intel
Download v1.0.15-alpha (macOS Universal)
claims.conditions: https://release.macflow.ai/MacFlow.dmg?v=1.0.15-alpha ; not downloaded, installed or verified as latest across all channels

claims.wording: MacFlow advertises workspace snapshots/export/import, dotfile tracking and baseline drift comparisons on launch.
claims.excerpt:
Snapshot your entire environment - packages, configs, dotfiles, apps. Export/import across machines. Git for your dev environment.
Auto-compare to baseline on launch.
claims.conditions: Not proof of exact reproducibility, complete restore, or cross-machine equivalence

claims.wording: Listed package integrations are Homebrew, npm, pip, cargo, gem and Mac App Store (MAS).
claims.excerpt: Homebrew, npm, pip, cargo, gem, MAS - all managed in one place.
claims.conditions: No package-manager version compatibility or provisioning test performed

claims.wording: MacFlow advertises targeted developer cleanup for brew, npm, pip, docker and Xcode caches.
claims.excerpt: Reclaim gigabytes from brew, npm, pip, docker, and Xcode caches with safe, targeted cleanup
claims.conditions: Do not repeat safe or gigabytes as measured/guaranteed outcomes; exact approval, deletion and rollback semantics not verified

claims.wording: The homepage advertises storage-growth alerts, CPU/memory/disk health views and exposed-secret scanning.

Storage Monitoring
Caches grew 4.2GB this month
Get alerted before your disk fills up.
Health monitoring (CPU, memory, disk), cache cleanup (brew, npm, pip, docker), security scanning for exposed secrets, and package update alerts.
claims.conditions: 4.2 GB is vendor illustrative copy, not an observed result. Process/helper grouping, writer attribution and alert runtime conditions not verified.

workflow.title: A Mac environment snapshot is not a storage cleanup plan
workflow.primaryIntent: Decide what to preserve before clearing developer caches or reproducing a Mac setup
workflow.reader: Developer maintaining packages and dotfiles across personal/work Macs
outline: Separate environment definition (packages/configs) from disposable, rebuildable and original data
Use MacFlow's documented snapshot/drift workflow to review package and dotfile changes; do not promise full disk backup or exact restore
Review cache scope and rebuild/download costs separately; no deletion recipes or invented UI steps
Choose environment orchestration versus storage/activity investigation; explain overlap without substituting one for the other
workflow.interactionPass: Plan a local decision checklist: preserve configs? need reproducibility? inspect growth? A snapshot is not a backup. No filesystem access, remote upload or forced code demo.
workflow.visualPlan: Official MacFlow workspace/app visual after lead only after rights and real UI inspection; labeled BR Space browser preview later.
workflow.linkStatus: Proposed counterparts; routes not verified or created in this job. Use only existing hub/tool links in drafting.

advantagesAndTradeoffs.tradeoff: Advertised alpha download; no restore/provisioning execution performed. Do not equate reproducible workspace with backup of projects or personal data.
